question: does the fitted basket behavioural direction change under native bf16 (RTX 3090) vs emulated (Tesla V100)?
restriction: two layers captured, so the argmax over the committed grid was NOT re-run; this asks whether the direction moved AT THE LAYER EACH COMMITTED AXIS SELECTED

residual_interpretation.CORRECTED_2026-09-21_S-177: The original artifact carried 'bf16_relative_precision: 0.0039' as the justification for calling the residuals float noise. REVIEW R13 showed that is wrong twice: 1-abs(cos) is SECOND order in the angle (theta^2/2 reproduces both residuals exactly), so it was being compared against a FIRST-order relative precision; and the activations themselves differ far more than that bound.

measured_activation_difference_rel_norm.note: ||h_new - h_old|| / ||h_old|| at site rel-6, 600 shared prompt_ids of 3714, seed 7

residual_interpretation.the_corrected_reading_is_STRONGER: inputs differing by ~2.6% in relative norm still yield fitted directions agreeing at cos 0.998 -- this is ROBUSTNESS of the fit, not agreement under noise.
residual_interpretation.the_verdict_is_unaffected: the 0.99 threshold was committed at 08:07:11, before the job existed; bf16 was the RATIONALE OFFERED FOR CHOOSING it, not the test. CLEARED stands.
residual_interpretation.the_preregistration_is_NOT_amended: configs/dcs_csi_pr009_basket_reextract_3090.json still carries the flawed why_0.99 rationale verbatim.
